cues.text: Hi Thomas, how are you enjoying the course so far?
cues.speaker: JEANNE

cues.text: Yeah, I think it's good.
cues.speaker: THOMAS

cues.text: Remind me why did you decide to study sports science?
cues.speaker: JEANNE

cues.text: Didn't you want to be a professional athlete when you were at school?
cues.speaker: JEANNE

cues.text: Yeah - that was my goal, and all my classmates assumed I would achieve it; they thought I was brilliant.
cues.speaker: THOMAS

cues.text: That must have been a nice feeling.
cues.speaker: JEANNE

cues.text: Mm, I thought I could win anything.
cues.speaker: THOMAS

cues.text: There was no one who could run faster than me.
cues.speaker: THOMAS

cues.text: Exactly - so what happened?
cues.speaker: JEANNE

cues.text: Did your mum and dad want you to be more 'academic'?
cues.speaker: JEANNE

cues.text: Not at all.
cues.speaker: THOMAS

cues.text: Perhaps they should have pushed me harder, though.
cues.speaker: THOMAS

cues.text: What do you mean?
cues.speaker: JEANNE

cues.text: I think I should have practised more.
cues.speaker: THOMAS

cues.text: What makes you say that?
cues.speaker: JEANNE

cues.text: Well, I went out to Kenya for a couple of weeks to train ...
cues.speaker: THOMAS

cues.text: Really! I didn't know that.
cues.speaker: JEANNE

cues.text: I was chosen to go there out of loads of kids and run with some of the top teenage athletes in the world.
cues.speaker: THOMAS

cues.text: And ... I was so calm about it.
cues.speaker: THOMAS

cues.text: I just kept thinking how fortunate I was.
cues.speaker: THOMAS

cues.text: What a great chance this was!
cues.speaker: THOMAS

cues.text: Everyone back home was so proud of me.
cues.speaker: THOMAS

cues.text: But once we started competing, I very quickly realised I wasn't good enough.
cues.speaker: THOMAS

cues.text: That must have been a huge shock.
cues.speaker: JEANNE

cues.text: I thought ‘this can't be happening’!
cues.speaker: THOMAS

cues.text: I was used to winning.
cues.speaker: THOMAS

cues.text: I'm sorry to hear that.
cues.speaker: JEANNE

cues.text: It's OK. I'm over it now and I think it's much better to do a university course and this one has such a variety of sports-related areas.
cues.speaker: THOMAS

cues.text: It's going to be good.
cues.speaker: THOMAS

cues.text: Oh, I agree - I chose it because of that.
cues.speaker: JEANNE

cues.text: So Jeanne - have you thought of any ideas for the discussion session next week on technology and sport?
cues.speaker: THOMAS

cues.text: We have to cover more than one sport, don't we?
cues.speaker: JEANNE

cues.text: Yeah.
cues.speaker: THOMAS

cues.text: You know - we always think technology is about the future, but we could gather some ideas about past developments in sport.
cues.speaker: JEANNE

cues.text: Look at early types of equipment perhaps?
cues.speaker: THOMAS

cues.text: Uh, I remember reading something about table tennis bats once - how they ended up being covered with pimpled rubber.
cues.speaker: THOMAS

cues.text: Cos they were just wooden at first, I'd imagine.
cues.speaker: JEANNE

cues.text: Yeah. In about the 1920s, a factory was making rolls of the rubber in bulk for something like horse harnesses.
cues.speaker: THOMAS

cues.text: Really!
cues.speaker: JEANNE

cues.text: Yeah - and someone realised that it'd make a perfect covering for the wooden bats.
cues.speaker: THOMAS

cues.text: So what about cricket - that's had a few innovative changes.
cues.speaker: JEANNE

cues.text: Maybe the pads they wear on their legs?
cues.speaker: JEANNE

cues.text: I don't think they've changed much but, I'm just looking on the internet ... and it says that when the first cricket helmet came in, in 1978, the Australian batsman who first wore it was booed and jeered by people watching because it was so ugly!
cues.speaker: THOMAS

cues.text: Wow, players have to protect themselves from getting hurt!
cues.speaker: JEANNE

cues.text: I mean everyone wears one now.
cues.speaker: JEANNE

cues.text: Mm, unlike the cycle helmet.
cues.speaker: THOMAS

cues.text: Well, unless you're a professional, but you're right, many ordinary bikers don't wear a helmet.
cues.speaker: JEANNE

cues.text: Hey, look at these pictures of original helmet designs.
cues.speaker: THOMAS

cues.text: This one looks like an upside-down bowl!
cues.speaker: THOMAS

cues.text: Yet, the woman's laughing - she's so proud to be wearing it!
cues.speaker: JEANNE

cues.text: It says serious cyclists ended up with wet hair from all the hard exercise.
cues.speaker: THOMAS

cues.text: I guess that's why they have large air vents in them now so that the skin can breathe more easily.
cues.speaker: JEANNE

cues.text: OK, so we've done helmets.
cues.speaker: THOMAS

cues.text: What about golf balls or better still golf clubs - they've changed a lot.
cues.speaker: THOMAS

cues.text: Yeah - I remember my great grandfather telling me that because a club was made entirely of wood, it would easily break and players had to get another.
cues.speaker: JEANNE

cues.text: There's no wood at all in them now, is there?
cues.speaker: THOMAS

cues.text: No - they're much more powerful.
cues.speaker: JEANNE

cues.text: The same must be true of hockey sticks.
cues.speaker: THOMAS

cues.text: I don't think so because players still use wooden sticks today.
cues.speaker: JEANNE

cues.text: What it does say here, though, is that when the game started you had to produce a stick yourself.
cues.speaker: JEANNE

cues.text: I guess they just weren't being manufactured.
cues.speaker: THOMAS

cues.text: So, one more perhaps. What about football?
cues.speaker: THOMAS

cues.text: Well, I know the first balls were made of animal skin.
cues.speaker: JEANNE

cues.text: Yeah, they covered them with pieces of leather that were stitched together, but ... the balls let in water when it rained.
cues.speaker: THOMAS

cues.text: Oh, that would have made them much heavier.
cues.speaker: JEANNE

cues.text: That's right.
cues.speaker: THOMAS

cues.text: You can imagine the damage to players' necks when the ball was headed.
cues.speaker: THOMAS

cues.text: How painful that must have been!
cues.speaker: JEANNE

cues.text: Yeah, well, I think we can put together some useful ideas …
cues.speaker: THOMAS
